case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated the 13th day of January, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4843 of 2000).
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Wahhab Miah J : This appeal, by leave, is from the judgment and order dated the 13th day of January, 2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4843 of 2000 making the Rule absolute.

2. Short facts essential to dispose the appeal are that one late Elahi Box Sarker made a Waqf of some of his properties under the name "Elahi Box Sarker Waqf Estate" (hereinafter referred to as the Waqf Estate) and the Waqf Estate duly registered on 17-10-1321 BS. As per terms of the Waqf deed, the Waqif became the first Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. Thereafter Fakir Ullah Miah, son of Nidam Nessa, the first daughter of the Waqif, Sabirullah Shah, son of Chetan Nesa, another daughter of the Waqif and Mostafur Rahman Chowdhury, son of Tayabatun Nessa, the youngest daughter of the Waqif, were appointed as Mutawallis in succession. Thereafter, the Administrator of Waqfs appointed respondent Nos. 1-3 herein as the Joint Mutwallis of the Waqf Estate on 1st April, 1998 for the alleged better administration of the Waqf property. The Waqf Estate owns landed properties in Districts, Rajshahi and Nawabgonj. Accordingly, the Administrator of Waqfs directed the Additional Deputy Commissioners (Revenue) of both the Districts to hand over the charge of the properties of the Waqf Estate to the Joint Mutwallis. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order of the Administrator of Waqfs, the appellants filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 40 of 1998 before the District Judge, Nawabgonj. The learned District Judge upon hearing the parties by the judgment and order dated 19 November, 2000 allowed the appeal and set aside the order of the Administrator of Waqfs holding that respondent No. 1 obtained the order appointing him and his two brothers (respondents Nos. 1-3 herein) as the joint Mutwallis of the Waqf Estate by practicing fraud upon the Administrator of Waqfs inasmuch as he suppressed the fact that the solenama filed on 14-9-1996 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 23 of 1991 was not proved and was not also accepted by the Court and the said appeal was withdrawn before any order could be passed on the solenama.

3. Against this order of the learned District Judge, respondent Nos. 1-3 filed the above mentioned civil revision before the High Court Division under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code). A single Bench by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute and set aside the judgment and order of the learned District Judge in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 40 of 1998 and thereby the order of the Administrator of Waqfs stood revived.

4. The High Court Division while interfering with the judgment and order of the learned District Judge observed that "For fair administration of the property in my view there must be common mutawalli". The High Court Division also observed that the administrator of Waqfs "also did so on 1-4-1998 by appointing the petitioners who were still Mutawalli of the portion of the aforesaid Waqf Estate fallen in the Rajshahi district and as such there should not be different administrators for the other part of the same Waqf Estate". The High Court Division did not also found the impugned order legal, "because the District Judge, Nawabgonj has not brought in to his consideration that the petitioners are the mutawalli of the Waqf Estate fallen in the Rajshahi district. So, for the benefit of the Administration of the aforesaid Waqf Estate the impugned order should be set aside and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Nawabgonj be directed to hand over the charge of the Waqf Estate fallen in his district to the petitioners who are newly appointed Mutawalli of the entire Waqf Estate by the Waqf Administrator on 1-4-1998".

5. Against the impugned judgment and order, Petition for Leave Appeal No. 490 of 2009 was filed before this Court and leave was granted to consider the additional ground to the effect:

"the High Court Division fell in error in reversing the judgment and order dated 19-6-2000 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 40 of 1998 being based on findings of fact arrived at by the Appellate Court to the effect that the respondent by practicing fraud and by suppressing the order number 54 dated 4-24995 by which the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 23 of 1991 was allowed to be withdrawn before accepting the solenama dated 14-6-1996."

6. Mr Probir Neogi, learned Counsel for the appellants having placed the order of the Administrator of Waqfs, judgment and order of the learned District Judge and the impugned judgment and order, has submitted that in view of the provisions of section 17 of the Code, the properties of the Waqf Estate in question having been situated in two different districts, i.e. Nawabgonj and Rajshahi, appeal under section 43 of the Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 (the Ordinance) could be filed before any of the two District Judges, i.e. Nawabgonj and Rajshahi. Therefore, miscellaneous appeal, in question was rightly filed in the Court of District Judge, Nawabgonj. Mr Probir Neogi has further submitted that since no procedure has been provided for in "the Ordinance" for disposal of appeal under section 43 thereof, the provisions of Order XLI of the Code shall be applicable in view of the provisions of section 141 of the Code. But the High Court Division failed to consider the above provisions of law in passing the impugned judgment and order. In support of his contention, he has relied upon the cases of Aminul Haque Shah Chowdhury vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury 4 MLR (AD) 367 and Amir Sultan Ali Hyder vs Md K. Alam alias S Alam reported in 29 DLR (SC) 295. He has further submitted that the High Court Division did not at all consider the finding of the Appellate Court that respondent No. 1 herein obtained the order of joint Mutwalliship from the Administrator of Waqfs by practicing fraud suppressing the fact that the solenama dated 14-9-1996 filed in Miscellaneous Appeal No.23 of 1991, was not proved and that before the same could be accepted by the Court, the appeal itself had been withdrawn.

7. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali learned Counsel, for respondent Nos. 2-7, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order.

8. Admittedly the appeal was filed before the District Judge under section 43 of the Ordinance and in the Ordinance, no procedure has been provided for as to the disposal of an appeal. In view of the provisions of section 141 read with section 108(b) of the Code, the procedure provided therein in Order XLI was applicable in the case of disposal of the appeal in question. In the context, Mr Probir Neogi rightly placed reliance upon the cases of Aminul Haque  Shah Chowdhury (supra) and Amir Sultan Ali Hyder (supra). And we also find substance in the submission of Mr Probir Neogi that in view of the provisions of section 17 of the Code, the appeal under section 43 of the Ordinance could be filed before the District Judge of either of the District, Rajshahi or Nawabgonj. So there was nothing wrong in filing the appeal before the District Judge, Nawabgonj against the order of the Administrator of Waqfs by the present appellant and the District Judge rightly decided the same.

9. So far as the merit of the appeal is concerned, from the judgment of the District Judge, it is clear that Miscellaneous Appeal No. 23 of 1991 was filed by respondent No. 1 against the order of the Administrator of Waqfs dated 16-3-1999 and when that appeal was pending in the Court of the Additional District Judge, respondent No. I as the appellant and two of his brothers who were respondent Nos.8 and 21 filed a solenama on 14-6-1996 with the prayer for disposal of the appeal (Miscellaneous Appeal No. 31 of 1991) in terms of the solenama. The learned Additional District Judge by order No. 43 dated 14-9-1996 kept the same with the record and fixed the next date on 28-9-1996 for hearing the appeal along with the solenama. Then upto 9-11-1997 adjournment was taken for hearing the appeal and the solenama and lastly the appeal was fixed for hearing on 4-2-1998 and on this date though the appellant, and the respondents were present in Court, the appellant filed application for withdrawal of the appeal and the prayer for withdrawal of the appeal was allowed on that very date, i.e. on 4-2-1998; thus it is clear that the appeal stood withdrawn before the solenama dated 14-9-1996 could be accepted. But by suppressing the last order of withdrawal of the appeal (Miscellaneous Appeal No.23 of 1991) the order of appointment of the joint Mutwalliship was obtained from the Administrator of Waqfs on the basis of the so-called solenama. The Appellate Court gave clear finding that the solenama filed on 14-9-1996 was not proved, and the same was not accepted by the Court and that subsequently the appeal (Miscellaneous Appeal No. 23 of 1991) having been withdrawn, the solenama filed on 14-9-1996 had no legal consequence and on the basis of the said solenama, respondent Nos. 1-3 had no locus standi to file application on 15-3-1998 and, as such, the appointment of the said respondents as the joint mutawallis by the Administrator of Waqfs on 1-4-1998 was obtained by practising fraud upon him; therefore, the order was liable to be set aside.

10. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, found it difficult to dispute the above factual aspect of the case.

<u>11. In making the Rule absolute, the High Court Division did at all advert the finding of the Appellate Court that the order of Appointment of respondent Nos. 1-3 as the joint mutawallis was obtained from the Administrator of Waqfs by practicing fraud upon him. The High Court Division also failed to consider the age old legal principle that fraud vitiates everything. The High Court Division also failed to consider that in view of the provisions of section 17 of the Code, the District Judge, Nawabgonj had the jurisdiction to hear the appeal under section 43 of the Ordinance though some of the properties Waqf Estate were situated in District-Rajshahi. In view of the above, the impugned judgment and order cannot be maintained and must be set aside.</u>

12. For the reasons stated hereinbefore, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and order is set aside and those of the District Judge are restored. The Administrator of Waqfs is directed to appoint Mutwalli in respect of the Waqf Estate in question as expeditiously as possible, not beyond 3 (three) months from the date of receipt of this judgment, keeping in view the terms of the Waqf deed and the provisions of law notifying the concerned parties and hearing them.

Office is directed to send a copy of this judgment to the Administrator of Waqfs immediately.

End.

full_judgment:
Borhanuddin J: This rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party nos. 1-3 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 31.08.98 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur, in Title Appeal No. 152 of 1994 affirming those of dated 16.07.1994 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Kachua, Chandpur, in Title Suit No. 43 of 1992, should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that opposite-party nos. 2 and 3 herein as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit no. 43 of 1992 in the court of learned Assistant Judge, Kachua, Chandpur, praying for partition of the Suit land contending inter alia that the suit schedule land originally belonged to Alimuddin Patwari, Moniruddin Patwari and Loni Patwari in equal share, i.e. 1792/3 decimals of land each; C.S. record prepared accordingly; Amongst them Loni Patwari died first leaving wife Meherjan (Mothi Bibi), three daughters Jobeda Khatun, Moyna Bibi, Achia Khatun and two brothers; Meherjan Bibi died leaving aforesaid heirs; Moyna Bibi died leaving only daughter defendant No. 21 Zaheda Khatun; Jobada Khatun died leaving two sons defendant no. 19 Charu Miah and defendant no. 20 Monjur Hossain; Thereafter Moniruddin Patwari died leaving wife Rupjan, two sons A. Majid, A. Sobhan and four daughters Rabiya Khatun, Ambia Khatun, Sabani Khatun and defendant no.42 Rownennessa; Daughters of Moniruddin Patwari sold 79 decimals of land to Alimuddin Patwari; Subsequently, plaintiffs and defendant no.4 purchased the land vide registered deed dated 07.10.1991; A. Majid died leaving wife Kamini Bibi, son defendant no. 1 Badsha, and three daughters Amena Khatun, defendant no.2 Julekha Khatun, and defendant no.3 Ranjani Bibi; Amena Khatun died without any issue; A Sobhan died leaving wife Halima Khatun, two sons. Plaintiff no.1 A. Khaleque, defendant no.4 Rafique Uddin, and daughter Plaintiff no.2 Tahera Khatun; Halima Khatun died leaving aforesaid heirs; Alimuddin died leaving wife Chand Bhanu, three sons Ismail Hossain, defendant no.11 Md. Younus, defendant no.12 Md. Ishaque, and two daughters defendant no.13 Joynad [Thane and Asiya alias Ashrafunnessa; Chand Banu died leaving aforesaid heirs; Ismail Hossain died leaving defendant no. 10 wife Karimjan, one son defendant no.5 Delwar and four daughters defendant no.6 Amara, defendant no.7 'fafura, defendant no.8 Jahanara, and defendant no.9 Rowshanara; Ashrafunnessa died leaving husband defendant no.14 Kazimuddin, three sons defendant no.15 Khorshed, defendant no. 16 Abdul Wahab, defendant no.17 Shahidullah and one daughter defendant no. 18 Samarat Banu; Ambia Khatun, daughter of Moniruddin Patwari, died leaving two sons Abdul Aziz, Abdur Rahman and one daughter Chand Bane; Said Abdul Aziz died without any issue; There is no trace of A. Rahman and Chand Banu; Moniruddin 1.13 Patwari inherited 18113/144 acres of land from brother Loni Miah and thus his total share in 65 the suit schedule stands 19865/144  dues of land; Ambia Khatun transferred a portion from her share to Alimuddin; Alimuddin inherited 8113/144 acres of land from brother Loni Miah and thus his total share stands 19865/144 acres of land; plaintiff's and defendants are the heirs of Moniruddin Patwari, Alimuddin Patwari and late Loni Patwari who are possessing the suit land in ejmali; Since the plaintiffs facing various problems in developing the suit land, demanded partition to the defendants who refused lastly on 20.02.1992; Hence, the suit.

3. Defendant nos. 1-4/21 and 42 supports plaint case and prayed for saham contending inter alia that Moniruddin was a co-sharer in the suit land to the extent of 1792/3 acres of land as per C.S. record and inherited .18113/144  acres of land from Loni Miah and thus acquired total 19865/144  acres of land; Moniruddin died leaving wife Rupian, two sons A. Majid and A. Sobhan, four daughters Rabeya Khatoon, Sabani Bibi, Ambia Khatoon and defendant no. 42; Rupjan died leaving two sons and four daughters; A. Majid sold his share of .43575/576  acres land by kabala dated 18.11.1942; After expiry of mother, A. 19. Heard learned advocates for the opposite parties. Perused the revisional application and annexures appended thereof along with lower courts record.

20. As it is stated above, no one appeared to press the rule but the opposite party nos.4-6/8/17 and 21 who supports the plaint case contested the rule.

21. It appears that dispute encircles regarding auction of Loni Patwari's share and purchase of the same in auction by Jamiruddin Pal. Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party nos. 4-6/8/17/21 argued that these opposite parties as defendant nos. 1-4/21/41 and 5-18 supports the case of plaintiffs contending that no auction was held regarding share of Loni Patwari and defendant nos.23, 28-36 failed to prove the auction by adducing credible evidence.

22. I have gone through the judgment and decree passed by the courts below. The trial court after elaborate discussions arrived at a finding that:

“এই বিবাদী পক্ষের দাখিলী কাগজাত প্রদঃ ক, খ, গ ও ঘ এবং প্রদ:- ট সিরিজ দ্বারা এবং বিবাদী গং ২৮ নং বিবাদীর স্বাক্ষ্যাদি এবং পারিপার্শ্বিক অবস্থা ও ঘটনা প্রবাহ দ্বারা লনি মিয়া পাটওয়ারীর সম্পত্তি নিলাম হইয়াছে এবং নিলাম কার্যাকর হইয়াছে মর্মে প্রতিয়মান হয় এবং ২৩ ও ২৮ নং বিবাদী স্বাক্ষ্য প্রদানে এবং কাগজাত দ্বারা লনি মিয়া পাটওয়ারীর সম্পত্তি নিলাম কার্যাকর হইয়াছে মর্মে প্রমাণিত হয়।”

23. And after reassessing the evidence on record, appellate court below disallowed the appeal and affirmed findings of the trial court holding that:

“২৩ নং বিবাদীপক্ষে দাখিলী প্রদর্শন-ঘ হইতে দেখা যায় যে, জমিরউদ্দিন পালকে জনৈক বছির উদ্দিনের নিকট নালিশী জমার .৯৮ একর জমি ২২/০৩/৩৭ নং তারিখের দলিলে খাই খালাসী রেহান দিয়াছিলেন এবং প্রায় ৭(সাত) বৎসর পর রেহানের দাবী পরিশোধ করায় রেহান গ্রহীতা দলিলটি জমিরউদ্দিন পালকে ফেরৎ দিয়াছিলেন। আগেই আলোচিত হইয়াছে যে, জমিরউদ্দিন পাল নালিশী জমায় লনি মিয়া পাটওয়ারীর অংশের সম্যক জমিতে নীলাম খরিদ মূলে মালিক দখলকার ছিলেন। সুতরাং প্রদর্শন-ঘ দলিল দ্বারা বুঝা যায় যে, তিনি তাহার উক্ত নিলাম খরিদা জমি হইতে .৯৮ একর রেহান দিয়াছিলেন। রেহানী জমি ফেরৎ পাওয়ায় জমিরউদ্দিন পাল নীলাম খরিদা সাকুল্য জমিতে মালিক দখলকার ছিলেন বলিয়া প্রতীয়মান হয়। এমতাবস্থায় ২৩নং বিবাদীর দাখিলী দলিল পত্র হইতেই ২৮নং বিবাদীরও ২৯-৩০/৩২-৩৬ নং বিবাদীর লিখিত বর্ণনায় উত্থাপিত লনি মিয়া পাটওয়ারীর অংশের জমি নীলাম হওয়া ও জমিরউদ্দিন পাল কর্তৃক নীলাম খরিদমূলে মালিক দখলকার হওয়া সংক্রান্ত দাবীটি ও প্রমাণিত হয়।”

<u>24. On perusal of the record, it appears that the courts below after thorough and meticulous discussions of the evidence on record arrived at a finding that the share of Maniruddin Patwari was not sold in auction. From exhibit-'Neo' and `Neo(1)' i.e. judgment and decree of Title Suit No.232 of 1984, it appears that in the suit it was declared that the compromise decree passed in Partition Suit No.32 of 1953 is collusive and illegal but there is nothing regarding auction sale of the share of Loni Patwari. The observation made by the learned Munsif in the case relating to alleged auction purchase of Alimuddin Patwari's share and after assessing the evidence learned Munsif arrived at a finding that Alimuddin Patwari's share was not sold in auction as such I failed to understand how exhibit `Neo' and Neo(1)' can help the case of the parties who challenged auction sale of the share of Loni Patwari.</u>

<u>25. Both the courts below after elaborate discussions of the evidence on record arrived at a concurrent finding that Loni Patwari's share was sold in auction and Jamiruddin Pal purchased the same. This finding arrived at by the courts below cannot be turned away for want of writ of delivery. The auction took place in the year 1921 and now we are in 2017. In the meantime almost a century has been elapsed. When there is a concurrent finding by the courts below on the basis of the evidence on record, this court in its revisional jurisdiction cannot held that the auction was illegal for want of mere writ of delivery of the auction held in 1921. It also appears that the evidences were produced and marked as exhibits without any objection. In the case of Jitendra Nath Mistry vs. Abdul Malek, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 106, our apex Court observed:</u>

<u>"The undisputed position is that the transfer by Ext B is being challenged not only after the death of the parties to the said document and that also after lapse of about 37 years. The plaintiff although has examined the aforementioned witnesses to establish the absence of the matters and circumstances necessitating transfer, but the evidence of the said witnesses is not of that level or kind to consider reliable for totally leaving aside the recitals in the document of about 37 years old. Had said document been challenged in the recent years of the transaction or at a time which is not as long as in the instant case and that had the transaction being not challenged alter the death of the parties to the document it would have been possible for the parties to the document and that also for the beneficiaries under the document to establish the recital relating to necessities stated in the document by calling them and that also other persons of the relevant time, but because of the lapse of time calling of the persons of the relevant time to depose about the fact stated in the document has become impossible as well as because of the death of the parties to the document."</u>

26. Apart from that it is settled position of law that under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure the High Court Division cannot re-appreciate the evidence and cannot set aside concurrent findings of the courts below by taking different view of the evidence. The High Court Division is empowered only to interfere with the findings of fact if the findings are perverse or there has been non appreciation or non-consideration of the material evidence on record.

27. Going through the impugned judgment and decree, I do not find any findings recorded by the Courts below are perverse and there has been non-application of mind.

28. Under the facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated above, I am not inclined to interfere with the findings of the Court below.

29. Accordingly, the rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

30. Order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby vacated.

31. Order of injunction granted by this court vide order dated 13.07.2000 is vacated.

32. Send down lower courts record along with a copy of this judgment to the court concern at once.
